title: Google DeepMind opens Genie 4 research preview with native audio and real-time steering
subtitle: The new world model generates explorable 3D scenes from text with simultaneous music, ambient sound and speaking characters, extends scene consistency to roughly two minutes, and is going to trusted testers ahead of a planned Google AI Ultra rollout.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4 on October 27 as a limited research preview for trusted testers, with planned expansion to Google AI Ultra subscribers and Gemini API developer partners. The model generates explorable 3D worlds from a text prompt and lets a user steer the scene in real time with keyboard controls and further text — changing weather, moving the camera, or inserting a person or object. DeepMind describes it as the first model of this kind with native audio generation: music, ambient sound, and speaking characters are produced alongside the simulation rather than layered on top. Scene consistency now lasts about two minutes, roughly double the Genie 3 ceiling announced in 2025. Reports describe the model as built on the Gemini family with Gemini Omni anchoring scene appearance and behavior. All output carries SynthID watermarking.

The capability that matters is interactive consistency, not visual fidelity. A video model generates a passive clip. A world model has to maintain object permanence, physics plausibility, and causal state as a user navigates — if you turn around and look back at a tree, the tree has to be in the same place, with the same leaves. Genie 3 could hold that illusion for roughly a minute. Doubling it is a meaningful step toward interactive content that is model-generated end-to-end rather than hand-authored. DeepMind cautions that visual details and object permanence still drift during longer simulations and after multiple complex edits, and that complex physical interactions, legible text rendering, spatial accuracy, and long-term consistency remain active research areas.

Genie 4 lands into a world model race that has quietly become one of the main competitive frontiers in frontier AI. OpenAI's Sora line, World Labs' spatial-intelligence models, and multiple open research efforts have each pushed interactive video generation and 3D scene synthesis in the past year. For Google, Genie connects to a broader stack: Gemini for reasoning, Veo for video, SynthID for provenance, and Genie 4 for interactive worlds. That stack is a plausible pipeline for everything from game prototyping to agent training environments — training embodied agents inside synthetic worlds has been one of DeepMind's long-standing research directions, and a model that can hold a consistent scene for two minutes is a usable training environment for short-horizon tasks.

A note for learners: if you want to understand where generative AI is going beyond chat, world models are the frontier worth watching. The hard problem is not making a pretty frame — image models solved that two years ago. The hard problem is making a scene that stays coherent across time, responds to agent actions, and obeys physical and causal constraints. The research that cracks that will underpin game engines, robotics simulators, driver-training environments, and the next generation of AI agents that need practice spaces. Open a Genie 3 or Genie 4 demo clip and watch for the moments when the model gets object permanence right — and the moments when it quietly rewrites the scene behind the camera. The gap between those two is where the next few years of this subfield will be won or lost.
